memory_update.text: AMKR should be retained as the US-listed OSAT reference anchor for the HBM/advanced-packaging overflow node; its thesis must be tested against AI/HPC advanced-packaging revenue mix rather than generic OSAT cycle exposure.
FORM is a strong underfollowed HBM-adjacent test candidate because company filings explicitly connect DRAM probe-card growth to HBM designs used in generative AI.

COHU is a small/mid-cap discovery candidate with explicit HBM inspection/metrology orders, but the current disclosed HBM revenue base appears small; survival in later layers depends on 2026 scaling evidence.

KLIC belongs in the speculative-underfollowed advanced-packaging equipment watch list; the evidence supports AI/CPO/heterogeneous-integration exposure, but HBM-specific materiality needs verification.

This pass did not include non-US-listed but highly relevant Asian names such as Powertech, ASE, Advantest, Disco, Tokyo Electron, and substrate/material suppliers; a separate non-US pass is needed for the full chokepoint map.

node: HBM, advanced packaging, OSAT, and backend memory-test overflow
summary: Expanded the US-listed universe around the HBM/advanced-packaging/backend-test overflow node. The cleaner underfollowed lane is not the HBM memory producers themselves, but suppliers and service providers one step below: OSAT capacity, HBM probe cards, HBM inspection/metrology, and thermocompression/heterogeneous-integration tools. The best-supported US-listed candidates in this pass are AMKR, FORM, COHU, and KLIC. AMKR is the reference US OSAT anchor; FORM and COHU have explicit HBM test/inspection evidence; KLIC is a more indirect advanced-packaging tool candidate tied to AI, CPO, heterogeneous integration, and high-bandwidth memory/chiplet assembly transitions.
